newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE barley futures close sharply down ahead of PRO.
newsitem.headline: WCE barley futures close sharply down ahead of PRO.

text.p: WCE western barley futures closed sharply lower to the $5.00 limit down on commercial and speculative selling ahead of the Canadian Wheat Board's Pool Return Outlook which should be issued later Thursday.
"A lot of people are looking for a decrease in the pool estimates (for wheat and barley) and are willing to go short into the report," one WCE feedgrain trader said.
Louis Dreyfus Canada was a featured seller, sources said.
November western barley finished $1.90 lower at $146.10 while July closed the $5.00 limit down at $144.50.
The CWB October PRO was due at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT.
Feed wheat futures were also lower with December sinking $4.30 to $171.00.
Canola futures closed mixed with November lower under pressure from hedge selling while other months were supported by commercial and commission house buying.
November ended down $0.20 at $406.00. The November crush margin fell to -40.95 from -38.06 on Wednesday.
Japan bought 8,000-10,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
November flax finished $4.50 lower at $362.50, December feed peas closed $0.50 off at $198.50 and December oats $4.30 easier at $126.50.
(All values in Canadian dollars except peas, oats).
